messages.content: 你能預測一間面積為2500平方英呎、有3間房間、建於2000年、位於紐約的房屋價格，並將其與一間類似的房屋但面積為3000平方英呎、建於2005年、位於洛杉磯的房屋價格進行比較嗎？最後，預測一間面積為2000平方英呎、有2間房間、建於1995年、位於芝加哥的第三間房屋的價格。

function.name: predict_house_price
function.description: Predict house price based on area, number of rooms and year of construction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

area.description: Area of the house in square feet.

rooms.description: Number of rooms in the house.

year.description: Year when the house was constructed.

location.description: The location or city of the house.

We need to call the function twice? Actually three predictions: first two houses (NY and LA) then compare them, then third prediction. So we should call function thrice. But maybe combine into one call? No each call separate. We'll produce output after calls.

We'll use the function. Let's do:

First call: area 2500, rooms 3, year 2000, location "New York".

Second call: area 3000, rooms ?, they didn't specify rooms count for second house. They said "similar" but only gave area, year, location. Probably same number of rooms as first? Might assume 3 rooms too. Or unspecified. Could ask clarifying question. But likely want comparison between those two predicted prices. Use default assumption: both have 3 rooms? I'll mention uncertainty.

Third call: area 2000, rooms 2, year 1995, location "Chicago". Then provide comparisons.

Let's proceed.
